text:
emma: FYI I've been debugging a flaky stream in the new sample-app where the first token sometimes repeats after a reconnect. Repro is short: start stream, crash client mid-event, reconnect with Last-Event-ID and sometimes you see the last token twice.
jay: can you share a raw tcpdump or the exact bytes the client receives?

emma: pasted capture: server sends:

id: 101
data: {"tok":"X"}

then soon after:

id: 102
data: {"tok":"Y"}

but the client read returned one read containing:"data: {"tok":"X"}
data: {"tok":"Y"}

then we aborted and reconnected with Last-Event-ID: 101 and server resends id 101. Node SDK ends up emitting X again.
carlos: this is classic: proxies coalesce writes and TLS/tcp don't preserve event boundaries. You can't rely on chunk boundaries.

emma: two problems we need to fix in SDKs for better DX: (1) tolerant parsing (accept single-LF or flush partial event after small timeout) so tokens are delivered quickly, and (2) dedupe on reconnect by `id` before handing payload to user code.
jay: for parity we should add the same behavior to Node and Go SDKs. I propose config knobs: `sse.dedupe=true|false` and `sse.partialFlushMs=number` (default 0 for strict behavior). Make them opt-in to avoid surprising strict users.

ops-bot: alert: sample-app-staging shows 0.9% stream reconnect spike around 2026-03-21T11:03:12Z :warning:

qa-bot: QA repro notes: nginx with `proxy_buffering on` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size` small reliably reproduces coalescing; also a client-initiated abort mid-chunk is easy to script.

carlos: implementation notes: dedupe by `id` is cheap: maintain a small ring buffer or LRU of recent ids (configurable capacity e.g., 1024). On reconnect, if event id <= last-seen-id skip delivery. Also garbage collect entries older than a TTL to bound memory.
emma: parser change idea: when we see a single LF (not double) we still parse fields and if `partialFlushMs>0` schedule a flush after that interval; if more bytes arrive before the timer we cancel and parse as normal. This gives low latency without breaking strict SSE semantics when needed.
jay: add an integration test harness (docker-compose with nginx/haproxy + tiny server that intentionally splits events mid-json and sometimes coalesces them). The test should assert: no duplicate tokens after an abort/reconnect and delivery latency below SLO when partialFlushMs is set.

emma: minimal client snippet I used to repro (Node fetch reader):
```js
const r = await fetch(url, { headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream' } });
const reader = r.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```
This shows merged frames in a single read.

carlos: also ensure SDK exposes raw `id` field to users or at least uses it internally for dedupe. Some customers rely on manual resume logic and need access.

ops-bot: action item summary:
- jay: open GH issues for Node+Go SDKs to add `sse.dedupe` and `sse.partialFlushMs` with tests (include suggested defaults and memory bounds).
- carlos: create integration test repo (docker-compose nginx/haproxy + server + client scripts) and add it to SDK CI pipeline.
- emma: update quickstart docs with a small section on Last-Event-ID resume behavior and recommended server flush configs for nginx/haproxy.
- ops-bot: scan hosted router configs for `proxy_buffering` and report any non-defaults.

qa-bot: I'll add an E2E that simulates abort+reconnect and asserts no duplicate tokens are emitted for both Node and Go SDKs.

emma: short-term workaround for users: include an incrementing `seq` field in event JSON and dedupe on application side, or set server to immediate flush on SSE endpoints. But SDK fix will make onboarding smoother.
jay: also include a metric `sse.duplicate_events` and a debug trace when dedupe skips an event so ops can see when servers are resending.
carlos: one more: document the tradeoffs in SDK docs: strict SSE parsing vs tolerant mode and how it affects resume correctness.
emma: PR with nginx repro and quickstart docs changes inbound, will link here when ready. :thumbsup:
